links.outcome: Local validation of published mortality scores on local historical data against observed in-hospital mortality
links.effect: Observed mortality 3.8% vs predicted 2.1% (EuroSCORE II) and 2.4% (ACEF); both poorly calibrated (HL P<0.001); EuroSCORE II AUC 0.774, ACEF AUC 0.638
links.quote: In-hospital mortality occurred in 3.8% of the patients and was considerably underestimated both by the EuroSCORE II (2.1%) and ACEF score (2.4%).

links.outcome: Calibration and discrimination after local recalibration of EuroSCORE II
links.effect: After recalibration, calibration good (HL P=0.79) and predicted mortality 3.2% vs observed 3.8%; AUC 0.777 not significantly different from original (P=0.92)
links.quote: The total mortality rate was slightly underestimated by the recalibrated EuroSCORE II model (3.2% vs. observed mortality 3.8%). However, calibration was still good (HL test P = 0.79, [ Figure 2 ]).

links.outcome: Differences between development and local populations and resulting miscalibration
links.effect: Local patients younger (53 vs 65 years), more critical preoperative state (9.8% vs 4.1%), more elective surgery (94% vs 77%); scores underestimated mortality in all risk groups
links.quote: The patients were younger (53 vs. 65 years), had lower creatinine clearance (74.97 mL/min vs. 83.6 mL/min), were more often in critical preoperative state (9.8% vs. 4.1%), and a higher proportion had elective surgery (94% vs. 77%) than in the EuroSCORE II population.

links.outcome: Generalization of predictive model to a new population
